title: EXP-071 - Hello World Part 4 Section 11a: Create the FX_Orders SQL Table and IDO with the Maintenance Wizard
objective: Follow hello-world-pt4.md Section 11 steps 1-4 (14:56-15:50), adapted to FX_ names, with the Web Designer New Form Definition > New Data > Maintenance wizard as in EXP-049. Prove the IDO FX_Orders and the SQL table dbo.FX_Orders absent and the dependencies available, then create them in one wizard run in FX_HelloWorldProject01 with Table Alias fxords and exactly four properties in order: FX_OrderNumber (Property Class FX_OrderNumBase, Primary Key, Required); FX_CustomerID (Property Class FX_CustomerID, Required); FX_Item (Property Class FX_Item, Length overridden to 50, Required); FX_Count (Data Type Long Integer, Label String ID FX_sCount, Default Value 1). The wizard Property Class lookup must list FX_OrderNumBase, FX_CustomerID and FX_Item; only if a class is missing, one Designer metadata unload (operator-authorized for this experiment) is allowed before one re-check. Verify the configuration, invoke Finish once, and answer No to the Create Form prompt (the FX_Orders Form follows in EXP-072). Check in the new FX_Orders IDO once if it is left checked out. Close and reopen the IDOs and SQL Tables Forms once each and recover both objects. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt4.md Section 11 (14:56-16:34) and its Orders schema quick reference, the EXP-049 record (wizard route, read-only Table Name, grid-editor intercepts, check-in, SQL Columns verification) and the EXP-070 record (the three property classes) before browser interaction; read EXP-044 only as needed.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-071-hello-world-part-4-section-11a-fx-orders-table-and-ido.md and evidence/EXP-071/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If it expires, follow the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure once and end the task. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection.

Collision gate: in the Web Client IDOs Form and SQL Tables Form, run one fresh exact-name query each proving FX_Orders and dbo.FX_Orders absent (zero data rows, visible criteria), with FX_Items and dbo.FX_Items as positive controls.

Dependency gate (read-only): FX_HelloWorldProject01 exists; in Property Classes, FX_OrderNumBase, FX_CustomerID and FX_Item read as in EXP-070 (FX_OrderNumBase Long Integer, AUTONUMBER(), int, FX_sOrderNumber, Right; FX_CustomerID String 30 nvarchar FX_sCustomerID with domain FX_HelloWorld01.FX_Code; FX_Item on FX_ItemBase with domain FX_Items.FX_Item). Change nothing.

Wizard: in the Web Designer open New Form Definition > New Data > Maintenance once (EXP-049 route); set IDO Name FX_Orders, IDO Project FX_HelloWorldProject01 and Table Alias fxords. With Site Split unchecked the Table Name is read-only and empty and derived from the IDO name on Finish (EXP-049); do not type into it.

Properties, in order: FX_OrderNumber with Property Class FX_OrderNumBase, Primary Key and Required; FX_CustomerID with Property Class FX_CustomerID and Required; FX_Item with Property Class FX_Item, Length 50 and Required; FX_Count with Data Type Long Integer, Label String ID FX_sCount and Default Value 1. Use the native Property Class lookup and commit typed values with Tab; record each resolved inherited value and any SQL Column Data Type the wizard shows or requires (the tutorial sets one for Customer ID; FX_CustomerID already supplies nvarchar).

Grid editors (EXP-049 rule): per cell, one editor-intercepted timeout is allowed; take one fresh snapshot and continue with the now-active editor of the target cell. A second intercept on the same cell, an unexpected value or any other timeout is a stop.

Lookup contingency: only if the Property Class lookup does not list one of FX_OrderNumBase, FX_CustomerID and FX_Item, record the visible list, invoke the Web Designer Unload All Global Form Objects once (Designer clean, wizard closed with its native Cancel first), reopen the wizard once and re-check; if a class is still missing, stop blocked.
Verify all four rows, their order, values, classes and key and required flags before Finish; invoke Finish once and record the completion message; answer No once to the Create Form prompt.

Inspect FX_Orders in the IDOs Form (project, table, alias, the four properties with their classes, effective values and the Count default) and dbo.FX_Orders in SQL Tables / SQL Columns (business column types, lengths, nullability, primary key, system columns distinguished).
If FX_Orders is visibly checked out after creation, perform exactly one native check-in of FX_Orders only and record the result; otherwise perform none.
Close and reopen the IDOs Form once and the SQL Tables Form once after clean states; recover each object with one fresh exact-name query and compare with the post-creation readbacks.

Capture screenshots of the gates, the wizard header, each configured property row, the four-row grid before Finish, the completion and Create Form prompts, the IDO and SQL readbacks, any check-in and the recoveries.
Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Classify findings as observed only.
out_of_scope: Creating the FX_Orders Form (EXP-072) or any other Form, and editing existing Forms.
Changing any property class, existing IDO, table, project, string, extension or theme; creating the FX_sCount string or other strings.
Any unload other than the single lookup-contingency Designer unload; any Web Client unload, FormSync, deployment or regeneration.
Checkout-management actions other than the single conditional check-in of the new FX_Orders IDO.
Creating records in FX_Orders or editing any runtime records.
Browser JavaScript, console or network inspection, direct URL navigation (except the portal step of the session-expiry procedure), refresh or restart.
Modifying earlier experiment records, AGENTS.md, tutorial sources, recipes or files outside the EXP-071 paths.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Never proceed if FX_Orders or dbo.FX_Orders already exists, a gate is ambiguous, or a dependency is missing.
Never modify a property class, an existing IDO or table, FX_HelloWorldProject01 or any string.
Never invoke Finish before all four properties are verified, more than once, or retry an ambiguous Finish; never recreate a partial object.
Never accept the Create Form prompt; answer No once.
Never invoke more than one Unload All Global Form Objects, never one in the Web Client, and never one unless a required class is missing from the lookup.
Never perform a checkout-management action other than the single conditional check-in of FX_Orders.
Never repair, rename or remove a partial SQL or IDO artifact if blocked; stop and report.
Never close a dirty Form or discard changes without operator approval.
Never click the Designer top-toolbar Delete button (Delete Form Definition).
Never use direct SQL, scripts, application internals or browser JavaScript.
Never refresh, restart or replace the browser session; re-login only through the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure, at most once per task.
Never run more than one recovery query per object after its reopen, or more than one close and one reopen per Form.
Never claim database durability or replay verification from same-session UI recovery.

target.form: New Form Definition > New Data > Maintenance wizard

acceptance_checks.description: Sources reviewed; session usable; Web Client and Web Designer clean; collision gate: FX_Orders and dbo.FX_Orders absent by exact-name queries with FX_Items and dbo.FX_Items positive controls. Evidence: query screenshots.
Dependency gate: FX_HelloWorldProject01 available; FX_OrderNumBase, FX_CustomerID and FX_Item read with their EXP-070 values; nothing changed. Evidence: read-only screenshots.

Wizard route and header: New Form Definition > New Data > Maintenance; IDO Name FX_Orders, Project FX_HelloWorldProject01, Alias fxords; Table Name read-only and empty. The Property Class lookup lists the three classes (or the single contingency unload is recorded with its reason and re-check). Evidence: header and lookup screenshots; unload count.

Exactly four properties in order with the specified classes, values and flags: FX_OrderNumber (Property Class FX_OrderNumBase, Primary Key, Required); FX_CustomerID (Property Class FX_CustomerID, Required); FX_Item (Property Class FX_Item, Length overridden to 50, Required); FX_Count (Data Type Long Integer, Label String ID FX_sCount, Default Value 1); the inherited values and any SQL Column Data Type recorded. Evidence: per-row and four-row screenshots.
One Finish with its completion message; one No to Create Form; no Form created. Evidence: completion and prompt screenshots.

FX_Orders readback in the IDOs Form (project, table, alias, four properties, classes, effective values, Count default) and dbo.FX_Orders readback in SQL Columns (types, lengths, nullability, primary key FX_OrderNumber); the conditional check-in performed once or not needed. Evidence: IDO, SQL and check-in screenshots.
The IDOs and SQL Tables Forms each closed once and reopened once; one exact-name query recovers each object matching its readback. Evidence: recovery screenshots.

The final EXP-071 report gives decisive evidence for AC-1 to AC-7, the complete action audit with exact counts (one Finish, one Create Form No, unloads 0 or 1 with reason, check-ins 0 or 1, Form close/reopen counts, recovery queries, zero changes to existing objects, zero strings created, re-login count), the worker-written-file inventory and the final state. Repository confinement is supported by worker/harness inventories, with operator git review authoritative. Findings are observed only.

initial_instruction: T1 - Read-only preflight for EXP-071. Review AGENTS.md, hello-world-pt4.md Section 11 and the Orders schema quick reference, and the EXP-049 and EXP-070 records. Without shell/git access, record the starting state concisely. List the browser tabs before selecting one; identify the Web Client and Web Designer tabs and their clean states. In the Web Client, run the collision gate (one exact-name query each for FX_Orders in the IDOs Form and dbo.FX_Orders in the SQL Tables Form, with FX_Items and dbo.FX_Items as positive controls) and the read-only dependency gate (FX_HelloWorldProject01 and the three property classes FX_OrderNumBase, FX_CustomerID and FX_Item). Create the EXP-071 record with the baseline, action audit and worker-written-file inventory, with screenshots under evidence/EXP-071/. Stop before opening the wizard.
notes: Proposed by the operator assistant after EXP-070 (accepted; Part 4 section 10 complete). Section 11 is split as in Part 2 (EXP-049 table/IDO, EXP-050 Form): this experiment creates FX_Orders and dbo.FX_Orders (tutorial Orders, alias Ords becomes fxords); the Create Form prompt is answered No and the FX_Orders Form follows in EXP-072. Properties adapted: Order Number becomes FX_OrderNumber (FX_OrderNumBase, PK, Required); Customer ID becomes FX_CustomerID (FX_CustomerID, Required; its class already supplies nvarchar); Item becomes FX_Item (FX_Item, Length 50 override, Required); Count becomes FX_Count (Long Integer, FX_sCount, Default 1). FX_sCount is referenced but not created (as FX_sCustomerID and FX_sOrderNumber). Unload: the tutorial unloads before the wizard; EXP-049 observed that the wizard lookup lists new checked-out classes without one. The operator authorized one Designer Unload All Global Form Objects for this section (2026-10-13); the brief uses it only as a lookup contingency. The single conditional check-in of the new IDO follows the EXP-049/EXP-044 procedure; the new property classes stay checked out. EXP-049 needed 18 worker tasks; the coordinator may need the same limit. Session-expiry re-login follows the worker preamble. deny_browser_javascript. Approved by the operator 2026-10-13 with precondition attestation: logged in, configuration OK, Web Client and Web Designer loaded, no unsaved changes.
